method_and_limits: measure_video.py keeps NUMBERS only: no footage and no per-frame skeleton is stored.

One camera angle only (side 3/4). 2D angles are the primary read; 3D world-landmark angles are reported alongside and differ by ~7 deg at the bottom. The comparison in REFERENCE_EVAL_2026-11-14.md uses the 2D-3D interval, not a single point.
The clip shows one lifter, 4 reps, light load (10 kg plates), no rack. Depth and tempo are representative of a controlled instructional squat, not a maximal lift.

Trunk lean and ankle dorsiflexion were NOT measured from this clip (the tool reports elbow/knee/hip only); the animation comparison for lean uses the design target and visual inspection, stated as such in the report.

purpose: Measured reference for the provisional Barbell Back Squat animation: one licensed video clip measured with MediaPipe, plus published squat-depth categories. Evaluation record only: this file does not make the animation approved.

reference_clips.assessment: TRUSTED: knee and hip angles at top/bottom, rep timing. Bottom knee interior angle: 2D median 57.4 deg (122.6 deg flexion), 3D median 50.4 deg (129.6 deg flexion), consistent across all 4 reps (2D 56.1-58.7). True bottom knee flexion lies in ~123-130 deg: the 2D value slightly understates flexion from the 3/4 camera angle, the 3D value relies on estimated depth. Hip bottom: 2D 57.4 / 3D 50.0 deg interior. Top: knee 2D 172.8 / 3D 162.6 deg interior. Tempo medians: down 1.12 s, up 1.22 s. Landmark overlay at the bottom frame was inspected visually: hip/knee/ankle landmarks sit on the joints. IGNORE the elbow values in the measurements file: the arms hold the bar and the 2D elbow angle collapses in projection (10-15 deg interior); they are an artifact, not a measurement.
